title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattnv2 + rotary/rope fused ops + kv-batching + scheduling
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/rope ops, add a KV-continuous-batching hot path and scheduler hooks to improve throughput and latency tail behavior for long-context and streaming workloads. Changes: 1) Integrates FlashAttnV2 kernels and implements a fused rotary/rope operator to eliminate redundant memory passes; 2) Adds a KVBatcher (continuous batching) codepath that groups KV updates across small concurrent streams and integrates with the scheduler to maintain SLOs; 3) Scheduler hooks allow policy-based routing to prefer fast kernels for low-latency tiers and fall back to compatible variants when memory quantization or hardware mismatches occur; 4) Introduces warmup and eviction heuristics for KV cache to reduce cold-start latency; 5) Adds Python bindings and microbench harnesses for reproducible perf measurements; 6) Compatibility: includes a tested legacy_fallback.cpp codepath and runtime feature flag (ATTN_USE_V2) to toggle at runtime. Benchmarks: On A100-80GB with 8x concurrent streams and sequence lengths up to 8k we observe end-to-end token throughput +28% on average and p99 latency reduced by 18% for chat-style streaming; memory usage reduced ~12% due to fused ops and fewer temporaries. Testing: unit tests for fused ops and kv warmup, integration perf suite in CI, manual validation against a representative customer workload. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout behind canary route; initial canary on dedicated clusters for two weeks with metrics: per-token latency, p99, GPU occupancy, NPU/FP16 correctness checks. Risks and mitigations: fallback path for models/quantizations not supported by v2, additional CPU overhead from batching coordination mitigated by lock-free queues and backpressure heuristics, and added CI perf gates to detect regressions. Follow-ups: refine batching thresholds by model family, add telemetry to trace KV hit-rate by prefix length. Related: ENG-3421 (attention perf), ENG-3510 (scheduler policies).
